note: Model versions change every few weeks. Each row lists the newest general-purpose release we found. Check the developer's site before relying on a detail.

sources.title: AI models released in 2026 (LLM Gateway timeline)

models.description: The models behind ChatGPT. OpenAI ships several sizes at once, from small fast models to large reasoning models.
models.uses: General chat, coding, agents that use a browser or tools, document work

models.description: Anthropic's assistant models, sold in tiers: Opus (most capable), Sonnet (balanced) and Haiku (fast and cheap). Ranked top overall in the MindsHub comparison.
models.uses: Complex reasoning, coding, long documents, agent workflows

models.description: Google's model family, built into Search, Android and Workspace. Gemini 4 Argon is a new top model that is only open to selected partners so far.
models.uses: Multimodal tasks such as video and audio, very long inputs, Google product integration

models.description: xAI's model, built into X (formerly Twitter). Known for live web and X search.
models.uses: Current-events questions, long coding sessions with web access

models.description: Muse Spark is Meta's first closed frontier model and powers the Meta AI assistant. Meta's earlier Llama models have open weights and are widely used by developers.
models.uses: Meta AI in WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook; Llama for self-hosted apps

models.description: Europe's best-known model maker. Many of its models can be downloaded and run on your own servers.
models.uses: European data residency, self-hosting, enterprise apps

models.description: Open-weight models that compete with closed models at a much lower price.
models.uses: Low-cost reasoning and coding, self-hosting, research

models.openWeights: Partly (Max is closed; many smaller models are open)
models.description: A large family ranging from small open models that run on a laptop to the closed Max model.
models.uses: Multilingual apps, fine-tuning a small open model, coding

models.description: The largest open-weight model released so far. Running it yourself needs datacenter hardware.
Open-weight models with a cheap, fast Flash version.
models.uses: Budget text and image work, coding assistants

models.description: Open multimodal models from the phone maker. The Flash version was rated best value in the MindsHub comparison, though slow and wordy.
models.uses: Low-cost multimodal tasks, on-device and self-hosted use
